• Nataraja is a depiction of the Hindu god **Shiva** as the cosmic dancer who performs his divine dance to destroy a weary universe and make preparations for the god Brahma to start the process of creation.

• The Nataraja sculpture represents Shiva in his form as the **Lord of Dance** (Sanskrit: Nata meaning dance, and Raja meaning king).

• Shiva is often depicted with a third eye on his forehead, a snake around his neck, the crescent moon adorning his head, the holy river Ganga flowing from his matted hair, and a trident as his weapon.

• He is often depicted as a youthful god riding a peacock and wielding a spear known as Vel.

• He is usually depicted with a dark complexion, holding a conch, discus, mace, and lotus flower.

• Vishnu is believed to have taken many avatars, including Rama and Krishna, to restore cosmic order.

• Ganesh, also known as Ganesha or Ganapati, is one of the best-known and most worshipped deities in the Hindu pantheon.

• He is the son of Shiva and Parvati and is widely revered as the remover of obstacles, the patron of arts and sciences, and the deva of intellect and wisdom.

• Ganesh is easily identified by his elephant head and is often depicted holding a modak (sweet) and riding a mouse.

question: In May 2023, the Supreme Court of India granted couples the right to get divorce on the grounds of ‘irretrievable breakdown of marriage’ under ______ of the Indian Constitution.
solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **May 2023**, the Supreme Court of India used **Article 142(1) **of the Indian Constitution to grant couples the **right to divorce based on 'irretrievable breakdown of marriage'.**
 
• **Article 142(1) **of the Indian Constitution reads, **"The Supreme Court in the exercise of its jurisdiction may pass such decree or make such order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it...".**
 
• The Supreme Court's decision expanded the grounds on which divorce can be sought in India.
 
• Previously, the grounds for divorce were outlined in** individual personal laws and did not include the concept of 'irretrievable breakdown of marriage'** as it was not explicitly listed as grounds for divorce in any specific legislation.** The 2023 ruling made it a valid reason to seek a divorce.**
 
• The court used its discretionary powers to take cognizance of the realities of irreparable marriages and rule in favor of allowing legal terminations in such cases. This action sets a significant precedent for future cases involving such marital situations.
 
• This step by the Supreme Court could potentially pave the **way for broader legal reform, rooting the law** more firmly in the changing social context and conditions of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 132(1):**

 
 
• **Article 132(1) **of the Indian Constitution is in **Part V **that deals with **'The Union.'**
 
• This article ensures that **crucial questions of law being decided by the High Court can be reviewed by the Supreme Court if necessary.**
 
• This helps maintain consistency in the interpretation of laws across the country and the** binding nature** of Supreme Court judgments.
 
 
 
• **Article 122(1):**
 
 
• **Article 122** of the Indian Constitution discusses the** "Courts not to inquire into proceedings of Parliament."**
 
• **Article 122(1)** states,** "The validity of any proceedings in Parliament shall not be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure."**
 
• The purpose of this provision is to uphold the **principle of separation of powers, an essential feature of the Constitution.**
 
 
 
• **Article 152:**
 
 
• Article 152 only defines the term **"Governor"** as referenced in** Part VI** of the Constitution, which deals with the states.

__
 
• The mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell because they produce energy in the form of ATP through the process of oxidative phosphorylation.
 
• They contain their own DNA, which is separate from the nuclear DNA, and ribosomes, which allows them to synthesize some of their own proteins.
 
• Mitochondria are involved in various cellular processes, including the regulation of the cell cycle and cell growth.

• There are two types of ER: Rough ER (with ribosomes attached) and Smooth ER (without ribosomes).
 
• Rough ER is involved in protein synthesis and quality control, while Smooth ER is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes**
 
 
• Ribosomes are the molecular machines responsible for protein synthesis in the cell.
 
• They can be found floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the Rough ER.
 
• Ribosomes are composed of RNA and proteins and are critical for translating mRNA into functional proteins.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Apparatus**
 
 
• The Golgi apparatus is a series of stacked membranes involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.
 
• It is often considered the cell's "post office" due to its role in trafficking molecules to their appropriate destinations.

question: Which of the following is the correct descending order of nitrate ion (NO₃^-), chloride ion (CI⁻), bromide ion (Br⁻) and iodide ion (I⁻) as per their basic strength?
solution:
The correct answer is NO3- > Cl- > Br- > I-.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The chloride (Cl-), bromide (Br-), and iodide (I-) ions are all halide ions and belong to the same group in the periodic table (Group 17, the Halogens).
 
• As you move down the group, atoms will increase in size and contain more electron shells, causing the valence (outermost) electrons to be less tightly held due to an increase in the shielding effect and a larger atomic radius, which leads to these ions being less attracted to hydrogen ions (H⁺), hence less basic.
 
• On the other hand, the nitrate ion (NO₃⁻) is less atomically extensive and is what we call a** "hard ion" due to its smaller size and higher charge density.**
 
• It features oxygen, which is more electronegative. The nitrate ion is also stabilized by resonance – the ability of the negative charge to be delocalized over several atoms reduces the reactivity of the ion (in terms of accepting a proton).
 
• **However, because of the smaller size, hard ions tend to form stronger bonds with H+ ions, so they are better bases than large, soft ions.**
 
• Therefore, even though NO₃⁻ is a stable ion due to resonance, it is still harder and smaller compared with the larger halide ions, making it more basic. Hence the order of basicity, from strongest to weakest, is: NO₃⁻ > Cl⁻ > Br⁻ > I⁻.

question: A 100 mL solution having 0.01 moles of NaOH dissolved in it. The pH of the solution is:
solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• pH and pOH: pH is a measure of the hydrogen ion concentration in a solution, while pOH is a measure of the hydroxide ion concentration.
 
• Relationship between pH and pOH: The sum of pH and pOH is always 14 at 25°C.
 
 
• pH + pOH = 14
 
• For a strong base like NaOH, which dissociates completely in water:
 
• NaOH → Na⁺ + OH⁻
 
 

**Calculations:**__

Given that,

__
 
• Volume of solution (V) = 100 mL = 0.1 L
 
• Moles of NaOH = 0.01 moles

The molarity (M) of NaOH solution is given by:

M = \frac{\text{moles of solute}}{\text{volume of solution in liters}}

M = \frac{0.01 \text{ moles}}{0.1 \text{ L}} = 0.1 M

Since NaOH is a strong base, it dissociates completely in water:

[OH⁻] = 0.1 M

pOH is calculated using the formula:

pOH = -log[OH⁻]

pOH = -log(0.1) = 1

Using the relationship between pH and pOH:

pH + pOH = 14

pH = 14 - pOH

pH = 14 - 1 = 13

**So, the pH of the solution is 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The pH scale ranges from 0 to 14, with 7 being neutral. Values below 7 indicate acidity, and values above 7 indicate alkalinity.
 
• Strong bases like NaOH have high pH values, typically close to 14.

question: Which element in the modern periodic table has the same number of valence electrons as that of caesium?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potassium** is the correct answer because it shares the **same number of valence electrons as Caesium.**
 
• Both Potassium (K) and Caesium (Cs) belong to** Group 1 of the Periodic **Table, also known as **alkali metals.**
 
• Elements in the same group of the Periodic Table have the same number of valence electrons - in this case, **one.**
 
• The number of **valence electrons remains constant** when moving vertically down a group in the Periodic Table.
 
• Valence electrons are crucial as they determine how an atom will bond with other atoms. **Both K and Cs, being alkali metals,** are highly reactive and tend to donate their one valence electron during chemical reactions.
 
• This is why the characteristics and chemical behaviour of K and Cs are quite similar. They both form +1 ions and have similar properties owing to the **same valence electron.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aluminium:**

 
 
• **Aluminium (Al) **belongs to **Group 13** of the Periodic Table.
 
• It has three valence electrons, which affects its** reactivity and oxidation states.**
 
• In chemical reactions, Aluminium often loses these electrons, resulting in a **+3 ion**, unlike Cs and K which forms **+1 ions.**
 
• Despite its difference in reactivity from Cs and K, Aluminium is widely used due to its **lightweight and resistance to corrosion.**
 
 
 
• **Barium:**
 
 
• **Barium (Ba)** is part of **Group 2**, also known as the **alkaline earth metals.**
 
• Unlike Cs and K which have a single valence electron, Barium has** two valence electrons.**
 
• This difference in the number of valence electrons makes it form **+2 ions** in chemical reactions.
 
• Barium compounds show a unique property in that they are very heavy, making them useful for **blocking X-ray and radiation emission**, as in Barium meal used in **radiography.**
 
 
 
• **Calcium:**
 
 
• **Calcium (Ca)** is also a member of **Group 2**, just like Barium.
 
• It has two valence electrons and hence, forms **+2 ions** in chemical reactions.
 
• Its chemical behaviour, influenced by the number of valence electrons, is thus distinct from Cs and K.
 
• Calcium is crucial for human health, particularly for the development and maintenance of bones. It's also an important component of the earth's crust; compounds such as calcium carbonate are found in rocks like limestone and marble.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Albert Einstein was a theoretical physicist who is widely acknowledged as one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time.
 
• He developed the theory of relativity, one of the two pillars of modern physics (alongside quantum mechanics).
 
• His equation E = mc², which asserts that energy (E) equals mass (m) times the speed of light (c) squared, is derived from his theory of special relativity.
 
• In 1921, he received the Nobel Prize in Physics for his services to theoretical physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect, a pivotal step in the development of quantum theory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Theory of Relativity**

 
 
• It includes two interrelated theories by Albert Einstein: special relativity and general relativity.
 
• Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity. General relativity explains the law of gravitation and its relation to other forces of nature.
 
• Special relativity introduced the concept that space and time are linked in a four-dimensional space-time continuum.
 
• General relativity introduced the concept of spacetime being curved by mass and energy, leading to what we perceive as gravity.
 
 
 
• **Photoelectric Effect**
 
 
• It is the emission of electrons or other free carriers when light hits a material.
 
• Electrons emitted in this manner can be referred to as photoelectrons.
 
• Einstein's explanation of the photoelectric effect was crucial in establishing quantum theory.
 
• He proposed that light could be thought of as discrete packets of energy, or photons, which was a significant departure from the wave theory of light.
 
 
 
• **Mass-Energy Equivalence (E = mc²)**
 
 
• This equation indicates that mass and energy are interchangeable; they are different forms of the same thing.
 
• It implies that a small amount of mass can be converted into a large amount of energy.
 
• This principle is the basis for the energy produced in nuclear reactions, where the binding energy of atomic nuclei is released.
 
• It has profound implications in both theoretical physics and practical applications, including nuclear power and atomic bombs.

• The sextant is a **navigational instrument used primarily to measure the angle between two visible objects.**
 
• The primary use of a sextant is in navigation, to measure the angle between an astronomical object and the horizon for the purposes of celestial navigation.
 
• The name **"sextant" originates from the Latin word "sextus", meaning "one-sixth".**

• An udometer,** more commonly known as a rain gauge, is a type of instrument used by meteorologists and hydrologists to gather and measure the amount of liquid precipitation (rainfall)** over a set period of time.

• **It is composed of several thermocouples connected usually in series or, less commonly, in parallel.**
 
• Thermopiles are used to measure the **temperature difference between two points, often the temperature of a surface and the temperature of the device itself.**
 
• **This difference can then be used to calculate the amount of heat energy received.**
 
• Applications of thermopiles** include gas leak detection, body temperature scanners, and industrial temperature measurement for kilns or gas turbine exhaust.**
 
 
 
• **Pyrometer Measures the temperature of a surface:**
 
 
• A **pyrometer **is a type of remote-sensing thermometer used to measure the temperature of a surface.
 
• The** term pyrometer was originally coined to denote a device capable of measuring temperatures of objects above incandescence (i.e., objects bright to the human eye).**
 
• **Pyrometers **are used in situations where** thermocouples are inadequate, such as in measuring the temperature of moving objects, objects in a vacuum, or very hot objects with temperatures above the range of thermocouples.**
 
• They are **commonly used in industrial applications such as steelmaking and ceramics production.**

question: A bus moving on a straight road at a speed of 10 km / h increases its speed to 70 km / h in 2 minutes. Find its average acceleration.
solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Average acceleration: The change in velocity divided by the time taken to change the velocity is called average acceleration.
 
• Formula for average acceleration: Average acceleration (a) is given by the formula:
 
 
• a = (vf - vᵢ) / t
 
 
 
• Where:
 
 
• vf is the final velocity
 
• vᵢ is the initial velocity
 
• t is the time taken
 
 

**Calculations**__**:**

Given that,

__
 
• Initial velocity, vᵢ = 10 km/h
 
• Final velocity, vf = 70 km/h
 
• Time taken, t = 2 minutes = 2/60 hours = 1/30 hours

So we have a formula for average acceleration,

a = (vf - vᵢ) / t

Substituting the given values:

a = (70 - 10) / (1/30) = 60 × 30 = 1800 km/h²

To convert km/h² to km/min², we divide by 3600 (since 1 hour = 60 minutes and hence (60 minutes)² = 3600 minutes²):

a = 1800 / 3600 = 0.5 km/min²

**So the average acceleration of the bus is 0.5 km/min².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Acceleration is a vector quantity that has both magnitude and direction.
 
• Deceleration is negative acceleration where the speed of an object decreases over time.
 
• In SI units, acceleration is measured in meters per second squared (m/s²).

question:
Which of the following statements about GDP and Welfare are correct?

1) GDP of a country is a indicator of welfare of the people.

2) If GDP is rising, the welfare may not rise equally.

3) GDP and Welfare both are not related each other.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

It reflects the total value of goods and services produced over a specific time period within a nation. A higher GDP usually suggests better living standards and economic stability. ***Hence, Statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **GDP Growth and Welfare:** Even if GDP is rising, it does not necessarily mean that the welfare of all people is rising equally. The benefits of GDP growth might not be evenly distributed among the population. For instance,** income inequality, environmental degradation, and other social factors can affect overall welfare despite GDP growth**. ***Hence, Statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Relation Between GDP and Welfare:** GDP and welfare are related, but they are not the same. GDP measures economic activity, while welfare encompasses a broader range of factors including health, education, and overall quality of life. Therefore, it is incorrect to say that GDP and welfare are not related at all. ***Hence, Statement 3 is not correct.***

question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India?

options.text: The original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court can be invoked by a certificate granted by the High Court.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The original jurisdiction extends to any dispute between the Government of India and one or more State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India has original jurisdiction in any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between two or more States.
 
• This jurisdiction is provided under Article 131 of the Constitution of India.
 
• Original jurisdiction means the power to hear and decide cases at the first instance, rather than on appeal.
 
• The purpose of this jurisdiction is to ensure that the federal structure of the Constitution is maintained.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 131 of the Constitution of India:**

 
 
• Article 131 grants the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between two or more States.
 
• This is a unique power as it is not shared by the High Courts or any other courts in India.
 
• This ensures that disputes of significant constitutional importance are decided by the highest court in the country.
 
 
 
• **Original Jurisdiction:**
 
 
• Original jurisdiction refers to the authority of a court to hear and decide a case for the first time, rather than reviewing a lower court's decision.
 
• In the case of the Supreme Court of India, its original jurisdiction includes matters relating to disputes between the center and states, and between states themselves.
 
 
 
• **Advisory Jurisdiction:**
 
 
• Advisory jurisdiction refers to the power of the Supreme Court to give advice to the President of India on legal or constitutional matters.
 
• This is provided under Article 143 of the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• **Certificate from High Court:**
 
 
• This refers to the process where a High Court certifies that a case involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution, allowing it to be appealed directly to the Supreme Court.
 
• This is provided under Article 132 of the Constitution of India.

question: Which of the following is NOT the feature of Fundamental Duties provided under the Constitution of India?

options.text: Duties are inspired from erstwhile USSR
Duties are non- justiciable in nature
Duties are enforceable by the law
Duties are intended to secure the country

solution:
The correct answer is __**Duties are enforceable by the law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties were incorporated in the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee, which was inspired by the Constitution of erstwhile USSR.
 
• These duties are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they cannot be enforced by a court of law.
 
• The primary purpose of Fundamental Duties is to remind the citizens of their moral obligations towards the country and promote a sense of discipline and commitment among them.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are intended to secure the country by encouraging responsible behavior among its citizens and fostering a spirit of patriotism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution deals with Fundamental Duties.
 
• They were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Initially, 10 Fundamental Duties were included in the Constitution, and one more was added by the 86th Amendment Act of 2002, bringing the total to 11.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are listed in Article 51A of the Constitution and are intended to serve as a constant reminder to citizens to uphold the spirit of patriotism and to contribute towards the nation's welfare.
 
 
 
• **Non-Justiciable Nature**
 
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, which are justiciable and can be enforced by the courts, Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable.
 
• This means that no legal action can be taken against an individual for not following these duties.
 
• However, these duties act as moral obligations and guide the citizens in their conduct.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**
 
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging impact on the Constitution.
 
• It introduced several changes, including the addition of Fundamental Duties and changes to the Preamble, among others.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee**
 
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee was appointed by the government in 1976 to make recommendations on Fundamental Duties.
 
• Based on its recommendations, the Fundamental Duties were incorporated into the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.

question: Which of the following statements regarding orographic rainfall is correct?

options.text: This precipitation is heavy but of short duration, highly localised and is associated with minimum amount of cloudiness.
This type of precipitation occurs when warm, humid air strikes on a mountain range.
This type of precipitation is characterised by seasonal reversal of winds that carry oceanic moisture.
It occurs mainly during summer and is common over equatorial doldrums in the Congo basin.

solution:
The correct answer is __**This type of precipitation occurs when warm, humid air strikes on a mountain range.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Orographic rainfall occurs when moist air is forced to ascend over a mountain range.
 
• As the air rises, it cools and condenses to form clouds, leading to precipitation.
 
• This type of rainfall is common in mountainous regions such as the Western Ghats in India and the Andes in South America.
 
• The windward side of the mountain receives heavy rainfall, while the leeward side (rain shadow area) receives very little.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Orographic Rainfall**

 
 
• Orographic rainfall is a type of precipitation induced by the presence of elevated terrain such as mountains.
 
• When warm, humid air is forced to rise over a mountain range, it cools and loses its capacity to hold moisture, leading to cloud formation and precipitation.
 
• This phenomenon is common in coastal mountain ranges where moist winds from oceans or seas are forced to rise.
 
• The windward side of the mountain receives heavy rainfall, whereas the leeward side, known as the rain shadow area, receives significantly less rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Types of Rainfall**
 
 
• **Convectional Rainfall:** Occurs due to intense heating of the Earth's surface, leading to the rising of warm, moist air which then cools and condenses to form rain. Common in equatorial regions.
 
• **Frontal Rainfall:** Occurs when warm air mass meets a cold air mass, causing the warm air to rise over the cold air, leading to cooling, condensation, and precipitation. Common in mid-latitudes.
 
• **Cyclonic Rainfall:** Associated with cyclones or low-pressure systems, where warm, moist air rises and cools, leading to cloud formation and precipitation. Common in tropical and temperate regions.
